turns.text: /navigator Grill me on how the request limiter in src/ works. Start with the basics.

Let's start with the big picture. The limiter in `src/middleware.js` gives each client its own `TokenBucket` from `src/limiter.js`.

First question: once a client has used up all of its tokens, what has to happen before `tryTake()` can succeed for that client again?
Tokens trickle back continuously, so with the default settings roughly one token is back after about 100 ms and the next request goes through.

Part of that is right: tokens do come back as time passes, and the bucket never holds more than `capacity` (`src/limiter.js` line 15).

The part that doesn't match the code is "continuously". `refill()` counts only *whole* intervals: line 13 uses `Math.floor(elapsed / this.intervalMs)`, and line 14 returns early when that is 0. With the defaults in `src/middleware.js` line 3 (`refillPerInterval = 10`, `intervalMs = 1000`), nothing comes back at 100 ms; all 10 tokens come back together once a full 1000 ms has passed. The test "does not refill before a full interval has passed" in `test/limiter.test.js` shows exactly this: a request at 999 ms is rejected, and one at 1000 ms succeeds. Line 16 also moves `lastRefill` forward by whole intervals only, so leftover time carries into the next interval instead of being lost.

(I inspected the source and tests; I didn't run anything.)

Next question: with the defaults, a client sends 10 requests at t = 0 ms and then one more at t = 1500 ms. How many tokens does its bucket hold right after that last request, and at what time will the next refill happen?
